requirements: Smoke detectors present and working
Carbon monoxide detectors present and working
Fire extinguisher mounted (on the 2023 form)
Water certification and sewer (septic) certification
Heating certification
Windows open, lock and have sound glass; doors in good condition
Plumbing pipes and fixtures, water pressure, water heater relief valve with floor discharge
Appliance venting and exhaust fans
Handrails and a 911 numbering pole
Emergency exit from a 3rd floor
Interior surfaces and interior and exterior paint; basement and firewalls; roof and chimney; porches, decks, stairs and railings
No mice, rats or roaches; clean property with a trash container
Electric wiring, outlets and GFCI outlets
Repairs found at inspection must be done within 30 days

resale_co.notes: No Township page says in one sentence that every home sale needs a certificate, but the Zoning Office fee list charges $75.00 for a 'Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Click for SALES form)' and $75.00 for 'Transfer of Ownership', warns of a waiting period to get a C/O on a previously owned home, and links a Sales Inspection Form covering houses, apartments and trailers; mobile home sellers must get a certificate of approval before sale. The two sales forms are scans (June 2023, and November 2022 marked revised 8/28/2023) and were read visually. The Zoning Office page names Clarence Dixon as Enforcement Officer (Tuesday to Thursday, 9 AM to 2 PM) while the Township Directory lists Mark Benjamin as Code Enforcement / Housing Inspector; the Directory is used here. Rental units must be registered and inspected every year (revised Ordinance 9-4); that is a rental program. Construction permits are handled by the Upper Deerfield Township Construction Office (856-455-9591). The live site only answers over plain http.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Fairfield Township as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: The Township's Bureau of Fire Protection page says the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's Fire Marshal's Office does the smoke/CO certification inspections for Fairfield Township, and the Bridgeton online application lists Fairfield Township. Fees, lead time and 90-day validity come from the Bridgeton Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025). The Township's own sales inspection also checks smoke and CO detectors and (on the 2023 form) a mounted fire extinguisher, although state law dropped the extinguisher from the fire certificate on February 3, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19).
